nodes.description: Address of the contract creator stored at deployment; used as the authorization principal and as the selfdestruct beneficiary.
Unsigned counter of the number of value-bearing deposits recorded by the contract.
Constructor that initializes creator from msg.sender and resets deposits to zero.
Payable fallback function that forwards any plain value transfer to deposit().
Payable entry point that increments the deposits counter when msg.value is greater than zero and returns the current count.
Constant getter returning the value of the deposits state variable.
Privileged function that destroys the contract and sends remaining balance to creator; guarded by an equality check between msg.sender and creator.
msg.sender read inside the constructor and written into the creator state variable.
msg.sender read inside kill() as the caller identity checked against creator before selfdestruct.
selfdestruct(creator) invocation that permanently destroys the contract and transfers its balance to the creator address.
Arithmetic operation deposits = deposits + 1 executed inside deposit(); subject to overflow if the counter wraps around.

edges.reason: The constructor writes the untrusted msg.sender value directly into the creator state variable.
An incoming plain value transfer hits the payable fallback, which immediately calls deposit().
deposit() executes the deposits + 1 arithmetic operation, the overflow-prone statement in the function.
The result of deposits + 1 is written back into the deposits state variable.
deposit() mutates the deposits state variable, incrementing the stored counter.
getNumberOfDeposits() reads the deposits state variable and returns it.
deposit() returns the result of an internal call to getNumberOfDeposits().
Reaching selfdestruct is gated by the msg.sender == creator identity check, making caller identity the access-control input for the destructive operation.
The creator state variable is passed as the beneficiary argument of selfdestruct, receiving the contract balance.
kill() conditionally executes the selfdestruct operation on the contract.
kill() reads the creator state variable to authorize the caller before destruction.
